concepts.definition: Secure baseline: approved hardened expected state
concepts.label: Secure Baseline

concepts.definition: Golden image: reusable template, not eternal state
concepts.label: Golden Image

misconceptions.claim: A golden image is permanently secure.
misconceptions.correction: Images age, dependencies change, and deployment context varies; baseline content requires review, patching, testing, and drift detection.

misconceptions.claim: Automation removes the need for approvals.
misconceptions.correction: Automation increases repeatability but still requires controlled identity, review, testing, authorization, and rollback.

outcome: Given a system change or drift finding, identify the configuration item and baseline, assess impact, select an approved correction, and produce evidence that the resulting state is secure and reproducible.

sections.body: Configuration management starts with provisioning and a complete inventory of configuration items and their relationships, followed by a desired-state baseline that records approved versions, settings, services, interfaces, identities, and dependencies. Provisioning should apply the approved state consistently and establish ownership, logging, and rollback evidence. Baselines can use hardened images, templates, or configuration-as-code, but they must be tested and maintained. Drift can be accidental, unauthorized, or an emergency response; detect it, classify it, and decide whether to remediate, approve, or investigate.
keyPoints: Provisioning creates or changes a resource; baselining defines the approved state it should produce.
Inventory must include dependencies and cloud or managed-service configuration where the organization is accountable.
Drift detection supports both security and troubleshooting.
sections.title: Provision from an intended state and detect drift

sections.body: Automation can provision, compare, and remediate configurations consistently, but an unsafe script can spread a defect at scale. Use version control, peer review, test environments, least privilege, protected secrets, approval gates, rollback, and post-change validation. Decide whether drift is a security defect, an approved exception, or evidence of an unrecorded change before correcting it. Document exceptions and emergency changes so the operational record explains why a system differs from baseline and when the deviation will be removed.
keyPoints: Automation needs its own identity, access, testing, and rollback controls.
Configuration documentation should explain dependencies and operational consequences, not only values.
Validation confirms the intended state was reached; it does not replace approval or monitoring.
sections.title: Automate repeatable correction safely

summary: Configuration management keeps systems in a known, approved, and recoverable state. Inventory, baselines, controlled images, automation, versioning, documentation, and drift detection reduce the gap between intended and operational security.

assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Actual configuration must be compared with versioned desired state and each difference dispositioned as authorized change, remediation, exception, or investigation. Correct drift through an approved path without destroying evidence of why it occurred.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The desired-versus-actual comparator and disposition gate let the learner trace each drift item to authorized correction, exception, or investigation.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

options.feedback: Changed fact: An emergency firewall change restores service but bypasses normal review. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Confirm the host and configuration item, assess whether the change is authorized and security-relevant, preserve evidence, and compare the state against the change record. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Record the change and reason, validate the resulting configuration, monitor it, and schedule retrospective approval and cleanup. Emergency authority can accelerate action without making undocumented drift acceptable.
options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged

options.feedback: Correct. Record the change and reason, validate the resulting configuration, monitor it, and schedule retrospective approval and cleanup. Emergency authority can accelerate action without making undocumented drift acceptable.

options.feedback: Changed fact: An emergency firewall change restores service but bypasses normal review. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Confirm the host and configuration item, assess whether the change is authorized and security-relevant, preserve evidence, and compare the state against the change record. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable state states: Production host is compared against versioned desired state Approved secure baseline; Observed diagnostic port is checked for authorized intent and impact Change record. The model keeps Production host, Approved secure baseline, Observed diagnostic port, Change record, Configuration pipeline, Verified resulting state distinct. Its changed case is “An emergency firewall change restores service but bypasses normal review.” and every option returns to a named repair state.
